claims.text: Replica-exchange or parallel-tempering molecular dynamics will capture the size-dependent thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles more accurately than conventional molecular dynamics.
Replica-exchange or parallel-tempering molecular dynamics will capture the melting dynamics of FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles more accurately than conventional molecular dynamics.
The initial materials are as-synthesized FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
The free-energy barriers associated with melting or phase transitions depend on nanoparticle size.
Enhanced sampling methods can overcome kinetic barriers that obscure rare events in conventional molecular dynamics.
Enhanced sampling can map the free-energy landscape of the nanoparticles accurately.
Mapping the free-energy landscape will reveal how nanoparticle size affects the distribution and heights of barriers involved in thermal transitions.
Smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles will have lower free-energy barriers than larger FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles.
Lower free-energy barriers in smaller nanoparticles will produce lower melting or transformation temperatures.
Conventional molecular dynamics may fail to capture the size-dependent melting behavior because it samples rare events insufficiently.
Conventional molecular dynamics typically under-samples rare events.
Under-sampling rare events leads to a less accurate representation of melting dynamics and size effects on thermal stability.
Enhanced sampling is most effective for nanoparticle sizes that are feasible to simulate with current computational resources.
Extremely small clusters or very large nanoparticles may have convergence problems in enhanced-sampling simulations.
Estimated free-energy differences and melting-temperature shifts depend on simulation parameters and limitations of the interatomic potential or model.
